title: Deeper/broader DXF parser screen and peer failure-lane reconciliation
mode: primary-source web research and read-only plan refinement
scope: Screen an additional DXF parser for material overlap with libdxfrw
Reconcile recent ACadSharp issue reports with existing local risk owners
Separate DWG MLeader object-context concerns from DXF MLEADER parsing
Refine peer admission and fast-validation readiness without changing support claims

method.kind: Read current upstream project documentation and issues, then map claims to the existing local plan
method.limitations: Mutable upstream README and issue pages were reviewed as peer-specific reports, not format authority. Full details for ACadSharp issues #1282 and #1283 were not independently available in this pass, so only their issue-index titles are recorded as leads. No peer behavior or local defect was reproduced.

sources.observed: The JavaScript project documents parsing text DXF into a projected object model and lists most 2D entities as supported, with 3DSOLID, some leaders, and other less-common objects not yet supported. The README does not establish DWG or Binary DXF support, arbitrary unknown-tag round-trip preservation, or ACIS/SAB semantics.

The report describes recursive stack growth for repeated comments, extended-data application blocks, and Wipeout clip-boundary data, including high-count reproductions and shared Binary DXF reader paths. These describe ACadSharp implementation paths, not a format limit or a libdxfrw reproduction. The local generated robustness lane covers repeated comments in ASCII, and XDATA plus Wipeout-like input in both ASCII and Binary DXF, with following LINE sentinels.

The issue index titles point to per-APPID EED size/overflow and nested-block deep-copy performance/stack-growth topics. Full issue details were not independently available in this pass. These are leads mapped to existing EED width/accounting and graph-work owners, not confirmed local mechanisms or thresholds.

The report describes an AC1032 DWG rewrite for which AutoCAD LT 2026 AUDIT reportedly rejects standalone AcDbMLeaderObjectContextData objects associated with extension dictionaries and annotation scales; it identifies two distinct serialization changes. The original source drawing was not available in the issue. This remains a peer report, not a reproduced libdxfrw failure.

The README presents version-level DWG/DXF read/write capability cells. These support route selection but do not prove entity- or field-level survival, graph closure, conversion fidelity, or solid semantics.

The recheck identified no new qualification claim to add: dxflib remains a callback-oriented DXF reference, and the original libopencad repository describes a narrow basic R15/AC1015 DWG reader and is abandoned. Existing plan roles remain appropriately limited.

assessment.planImpact: Screened dxf-parser out as a general parity dependency and 3D comparator; mapped peer-reported recursion, EED-width, nested-block-work, and AC1032 MLeader-context risks to existing owners; kept the DWG object-context report distinct from DXF MLEADER parsing; and reiterated exact operation overlap, generated local reproduction, and focused fast validation as implementation-readiness gates.

implementationReadyChecks: Treat a peer issue as a hypothesis until the matching local path, format/version/direction, invariant, and independently expected generated reproduction are named.
For repeated DXF inputs, use the owning focused selector with bounded progress and a following-record sentinel; do not import peer count thresholds.
Route EED width/accounting and nested-block work to their existing owners; do not infer limits or performance thresholds from issue titles alone.
Keep AC1032 DWG MLeader object-context closure separate from DXF MLEADER groups and qualify it at the composed object-graph/native-AUDIT gate.
Do not add dxf-parser as a dependency; an optional future ASCII comparison requires an exact artifact/runtime and independently authored expected fields.
No broad suite, peer build, sanitizer campaign, external fixture, or native CAD run is required for this research-only update.
